== Sounio ==

{{works with|Sounio|v1.0.0-beta.6}}

Sounio has no exceptions. Errors are returned as integer codes in tuples. The convention is <code>(value, 0)</code> for success and <code>(zero_value, error_code)</code> for failure.

<lang sounio>fn safe_divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> (f64, i32) with Div, Panic {
    if b == 0.0 { (0.0, 1) }    // error: division by zero
    else { (a / b, 0) }          // success
}

fn safe_sqrt(x: f64) -> (f64, i32) {
    extern "C" { fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 }
    if x < 0.0 { (0.0, 2) }     // error: negative input
    else { (sqrt(x), 0) }
}

fn main() with IO, Div, Panic {
    let (result, err) = safe_divide(10.0, 2.0)
    if err == 0 { println(result) }
    else { println("divide error") }

    let (result2, err2) = safe_divide(10.0, 0.0)
    if err2 == 0 { println(result2) }
    else { println("divide error") }

    let (result3, err3) = safe_sqrt(0 - 4.0)
    if err3 == 0 { println(result3) }
    else { println("sqrt error: negative input") }
}</lang>

Output:
<pre>5.0
divide error
sqrt error: negative input</pre>

Note: Sounio uses tuple destructuring for error handling. There is no <code>try</code>/<code>catch</code>, no <code>Result<T,E></code> sugar, and no <code>?</code> operator — error propagation is explicit.
